title: Experts Call Government's Earthquake Response "Completely Ineffective"
detail: A week after the earthquakes, PBS NewsHour reported that Venezuela's disaster response was hampered by years of hollowed-out institutional capacity: firefighters lacked fuel, civil defense workers searched rubble using cellphone flashlights, and citizens and volunteers organized rescue efforts before state agencies arrived. Foreign aid faced bureaucratic friction — a German emergency medical team was denied entry, Colombian firefighters were delayed for hours without clearance, and Chilean rescue workers faced documentation checks while working, while access to hard-hit La Guaira required registration. Phil Gunson of the International Crisis Group said the government "doesn't appear to have given any thought to what would happen in an earthquake"; Orlando Pérez of the University of North Texas at Dallas said "six months is not enough time to rebuild institutions that took two decades to hollow out"; and WOLA's Laura Cristina Dib said the response "left citizens in a situation of deep vulnerability." Foreign Policy separately described the failed response as the sharpest test yet of Acting President Rodríguez's leadership.

media.caption: Rescue teams continue searching collapsed buildings a week after Venezuela's earthquakes

title: Machado's Push to Return for Quake Relief Draws Trump Administration Rebuke
detail: María Corina Machado's repeated attempts to return to Venezuela after the earthquakes — including a bid to play a role administering aid — angered senior Trump administration officials, who called her efforts "grotesque political opportunism" and said they saddled the State Department with "extra needless drama." Machado, who has been living in the U.S. on an expired Venezuelan passport since the White House sidelined her in January in favor of working with Rodríguez's transitional government, has lobbied Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Deputy Secretary of State Chris Landau, Miami-area Republican members of Congress, and White House officials for permission to return. The episode deepened an emerging rift between GOP hawks sympathetic to Machado and a Trump administration that has continued backing Rodríguez.

media.caption: Trump administration officials rebuke Machado's efforts to return to Venezuela after the earthquakes
